Thanks again for the SIG+CAIQ packet you shared last week. Our procurement & security team are running a residency/escrow reconciliation for EU-facing deployments and had a few follow-ups we hoped you could clarify quickly:

1) Can you confirm which subprocessors may persist customer data outside the EU for longer than 30 days? We only need the short list and locations (country-level).

3) For escrow/incident-runbook purposes: can Redwood provide a signed attestation (PDF) that describes custody paths and a CSV export of the current subprocessor roster reflecting residency, purpose, and last updated timestamp?

We'd ideally have these items by Tuesday 2-Sep to close our SIG review. If anything requires a DPA amendment or additional paperwork we can route that through procurement.

Appreciate the help — Ellen

Vanessa,

I pulled the latest roster and ran the residency flag. Attached is a filtered CSV (redwood_subprocessor_inventory_2025-08.csv) with columns: provider_name, country_of_residency, purpose, data_scope, last_updated. Short summary:
- 4 providers show EU residency only (DE, IE, NL)
- 2 providers (edge-accel-cdn, logging-archive) have primary residency in US; neither persist raw customer content beyond our 14-day retention window in normal ops, but the logging-archive has a 90-day backup window for crash recovery.

On KMS: our per-request ephemeral keys are generated with a 60-second TTL for inferred session keys. The long-term KMS key material (root key) is stored in our HSM (AWS KMS + customer-controlled CMKs for dedicated/private). No subprocessor has access to unwrapped root key material. The logging-archive team does receive encrypted telemetry blobs but never unwrapped keys.

I also exported the CSV and uploaded it to the shared Drive folder (link to follow). I can redact provider contact info if Ellen requests.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_2025-08.csv
